model_b.text: OBJECTIVE To investigate the effect of sulforaphane on apoptosis in renal tubular epithelial cells (HK-2) and its role in modulating the activation of the endoplasmic reticulum stress IRE-1/JNK signaling pathway. METHODS An in vitro HK-2 cell injury model was induced using uric acid (200 mg/L). The cells were divided into the following groups: control group, uric acid group (HK-2 cells treated with 200 mg/L uric acid for 24 h), low-dose sulforaphane group (HK-2 cells co-treated with 200 mg/L uric acid and 10 μM sulforaphane for 24 h), medium-dose sulforaphane group (HK-2 cells co-treated with 200 mg/L uric acid and 20 μM sulforaphane for 24 h), and high-dose sulforaphane group (HK-2 cells co-treated with 200 mg/L uric acid and 40 μM sulforaphane for 24 h). The proliferative activity of HK-2 cells was analyzed using the CCK8 assay, apoptosis rate was measured by flow cytometry, and protein expression levels of Cleaved caspase 3, Cleaved caspase 12, BiP/GRP78, IRE-1, and JNK were determined by Western blot. RESULTS Compared with the control group, the uric acid group showed significantly reduced relative cell viability (P < 0.05), increased apoptosis rate (P < 0.05), and elevated protein expression of Cleaved caspase 3, Cleaved caspase 12, BiP/GRP78, IRE-1, and JNK (P < 0.05). Compared with the uric acid group, the sulforaphane-treated groups at different concentrations exhibited significantly increased relative cell viability (P < 0.05), decreased apoptosis rate (P < 0.05), and downregulated expression of Cleaved caspase 3, Cleaved caspase 12, BiP/GRP78, IRE-1, and JNK (P < 0.05). CONCLUSION Sulforaphane reduces apoptosis in renal tubular epithelial cells by inhibiting the activation of the endoplasmic reticulum stress IRE-1/JNK signaling pathway.
